statement: The Kalmar Union (1397–1523), established by Queen Margaret I of Denmark (regent for her grandnephew Eric of Pomerania), united Denmark, Norway, and Sweden under a single crown while preserving each kingdom's laws and institutions. Margaret I effectively governed all three until her death (1412). The union was plagued by Swedish resistance to Danish dominance; Engelbrekt Engelbrektsson's revolt (1434) began the cycle of Swedish separatism that culminated in the Stockholm Bloodbath (1520) and the definitive Swedish exit under Gustav Vasa (1523).
